articles.title: The Battlestar Galactica Board Game Is Making a Surprise Comeback Next Year
articles.body:
When it comes to board games, a frequent “Holy Grail” game (a term used to describe a game that someone has been hunting for, usually out of print and expensive) on many lists is Fantasy Flight Games’ Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game. But it looks like the search may be coming to an end for fans, as it was announced today that Ghost Galaxy has entered into an agreement with Universal and Fantasy Flight Games to publish a brand-new edition of this coveted title, coming to crowdfunding early next year.

First released back in 2008 and featuring imagery from the Sci-Fi Channel reboot , this social deduction/hidden traitor game wonderfully captured the tension from the show, where anyone could be a secret Cylon agent trying to thwart the single mission of the humans—to get home. Battlestar Galactica would go on to get three expansions, but almost a decade ago now, it all went out of print, and now prices on the secondary market for a full set (base game + expansions) could easily cost you more than a grand. Back in 2021, FFG did release a sort of reskinned version of BSG with Unfathomable, which replaced the Galactica with a boat and the Cylons with Lovecraftian horrors, which has seen success as well.

Details on this new edition are scant right now; all we have is that it’s a “new edition” that will feature “an updated design,” whatever that means, but I think the game is in safe hands. Overseeing this project will be Christian T. Peterson, the CEO of Ghost Galaxy and formerly the founder and CEO of Fantasy Flight Games and the creator of a little game called Twilight Imperium.

Recently, Fantasy Flight Games launched a similar campaign as the debut of its “Vault Series” with Arkham Horror Remastered (check out our interview and exclusive art reveal ), which seeks to accomplish a similar goal with the much-loved Arkham Horror Second Edition. Whether this will be a part of the Vault Series or not, seeing as it is being officially published by another group, remains to be seen, but awesome to hear nonetheless.

The campaign page for the new edition of Battlestar Galactica will be launching soon, so you and your wallet can rejoice.

Scott White is a freelance contributor to IGN, assisting with tabletop games and guide coverage. Follow him on X/Twitter or Bluesky .

articles.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Episodes 7-9 Bring the Lore and Laughter
articles.summary: Avatar: Seven Havens Episodes 7-9 recap and review: Lore and laughter dominate the latest episodes of the series.
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Avatar: Seven Havens Season 1, Episodes 7-9!

Whoa, doggy (and we can say that because non-hybrid dogs exist in the world of Avatar)1 After last week’s episodes of Seven Havens seemed to settle into a nice, comfortable rhythm, this week’s trio literally and figuratively tossed the table with some huge story moves and big additions to the mythology while somehow also managing to be the most effortlessly funny episodes thus far. At least a portion of that is due to the show’s first two-part episode, which you know has to be big — and it is — but thanks to the continued impressive balance of ongoing mysteries and emotional storytelling, Episodes 7-9 are a thrilling roller-coaster ride from start to finish.

Oh, and also we get to see Korra and Asami again, so commence freaking out, everyone!

To talk broad strokes before we get into the specifics of the episodes: As we’ve stated in previous recaps, the metaphor Seven Havens seems to be going for is how in our own world, countries are closing borders and refusing to work with each other to fix larger problems — i.e. the environment — while also amping up fear of the other. In this case, that “other” are the Havens other than Ellora, which is the main one we’re spending time in this season. But it also extends to the ostensible villains — raiders known as the Faceless, and more specifically the Avatar, as for hundreds of years people have believed Korra caused the Cataclysm that wrecked the world.

This week, with Envoys visiting from other Havens (more on that below), we get to see this distrust in action. It’s enormously simplified for the child’s cartoon we’re watching (no shade there) to the other Havens needing food and Ellora wanting benders to protect them from the red diamond Anomaly that has been growing and attacking Ellora at a regular rate. We’re not talking complicated, multi-faceted trade deals here, and that’s fine. But the thrust is clear for the viewer: These Havens, of course, would be stronger together, but it’s easier to give in to fear, the real theme of this season, than join up. Alone, the Havens are in survival mode; together, they might have something greater, but through pride, tradition, or whatever excuse they want to give, it doesn’t happen.

And for any viewers frustrated about these moves, there’s a key moment late in Episode 9, “The Envoys: Part Two,” when Commander Karthik (Akshay Khanna) talks about how they were raised to hate the Avatar. While it’s been a decade or so in our time since we’ve last seen the Avatar, and we know that Pavi (Saheli Khan) and Nisha (Aishu Devan), our twin Avatars, are good, It’s been 225 years since Avatar: The Legend of Korra. That’s over two centuries, and every character we’re watching on TV was born and raised in a world that doesn’t just hate and fear the Avatar, but has also been taught to distrust each other. Heck, their parents, grandparents, and probably even great-grandparents were born and raised the same. They don’t know any other life, and society has developed solely based around these precepts. It’s less about breaking programming than completely reconceptualizing history and learning. That’s hard, folks!

And speaking of Karthik, let’s take a small but related side-trip to talk about what happens towards the end of Episode 9. Pretty much since he first popped up, fans have pointed at Karthik as likely turning evil, getting corrupted, or perhaps being the head of the evil (or at least morally grey) Red Lotus instead of the Order of the White Lotus, which turns out to be 100% totally not true. In fact, in a shocker, it’s Jae (Major Curda) who betrays Karthik and the Avatars. We’ve watched Jae struggle with what we mentioned above, being raised in a society where the Avatar is seen as the ultimate evil. In Episode 9, he does turn against them, tells everyone about the White Lotus, gets Karthik arrested, and becomes Commander of the Bending Brigade himself. While it’s possible this might be revealed as a long range plan to do the right thing, at least at the end of this week, it’s a punch in the gut, and a real emotional surprise to see a character we’ve been following and believed in stick to the status quo instead of growing, changing, and learning.

It’s also, to be clear, very smartly done and more realistic: In real life, people rarely break out of their programming; they may be challenged, and they could even flirt with changing their minds, but sadly, more often than not they stay with what’s comfortable rather than truly evolve. So, boo to Jae! Hooray to the writers of Seven Havens. Also, boo to the writers — how dare you do this to Jae?! Life is complicated.

Anyway, there’s lots more to get into, so let’s do some brief recap. First up is Episode 7, “What Lies Beneath,” which does not include appearances by either Harrison Ford* or Michelle Pfeiffer. Instead, when Pavi decides to try and connect with the Anomaly to try and chase down more memories of her missing parents, she blasts a hole in the massive red crystal, revealing tunnels under Ellora. It turns out there’s a lot under the city, including a factory that was built by none other than Asami Sato. Thanks to a “mover,” we get to see both Korra and Asami, older, happier, and not in the Spirit World (where we last left them at the end of Legend of Korra).

(*What kind of bender do you think Ford would be? Is there cranky old man bending? Is that a thing?)

Also lying beneath? The Faceless, who we discover are aiming to live free rather than have life prescribed for them by the dictates of Ellora. Specifically, if you have bending ability, you join the Bending Brigade. That’s what Jae wants and what he believes in, but not Uki (Kimberly Woods), who was seemingly kidnapped last week but has actually been part of the Faceless the whole time. She leads Jae to the Faceless Queen, Zi (Dianne Doan), who later turns out not to be the Faceless Queen, though we’ll get there in a second.

That’s because so many other things happen in this episode! Pavi, first of all, discovers a bubbling pit of red energy, which grabs her and transports her back to Republic City, where we see the beginning of the Cataclysm. It sure looks like Korra in the Avatar state is tearing Republic City to the ground while releasing Spirit Energy tentacles. She’s definitely not, of course, and we’ll likely get a lot more info on this in subsequent episodes and seasons. But it confirms the suspicion that a lot of theories have rested on, and without getting too in the weeds on this: Back at the end of Legend of Korra, the doors between the Spirit and Human world were still open, and there was a lot of controversy about the use of Spirit Energy as batteries (think nuclear energy and you have the general idea). Given the Avatar is always about finding balance in the world, it’s probably fair to posit based on this one scene that things became very out of balance because of Republic City using Spirit Vine energy. Korra tried to stop it, and possibly the Spirit World crashed into the Human world.

We discover that the song Pavi and Nisha remember being sung by their parents is sung by people from the Eastern Outskirts in a lovely little moment where Uki pauses their tense showdown to offer up info on the ditty. Pavi and Nisha have a rift growing between them, and we end with two groups of Envoys — one from New Ba Sing Se and the other from Akasha — travelling towards Ellora like an Avatar version of Mad Max: Fury Road. We just needed Chong wailing on his dramyin while flames pump in the background to complete the picture. So shiny. So chrome!

Then it’s time for the two-parter, “The Envoys.” In the first part, the focus is on the summit between New Ba Sing Se, Akasha, and Ellora, which gets broken up by an attack by the Faceless, revealing the Faceless Queen is none other than… Agam (Sakina Jaffrey), the friendly cook/baker who has now not-so-curiously shown up in nearly every episode. Meanwhile, Nisha gets tested by the White Lotus representatives from New Ba Sing Se, Akasha, and what sounds like Nutha (NOTE: there are no closed captions on the screeners provided by Paramount+, so we might have the spelling wrong)... and fails.

That leads us into the game-changing second part, which doesn’t have a cold open before the title sequence, so you know it’s a big one. We almost immediately discover Agam’s motivation: Her father was taken against his will as a bender in the Brigade. In response, Agam created the Faceless as a way of being free and following their own destiny. Her destiny? To lead them to Republic Forest, which functions not just as a complete recontextualization of the main location in Legend of Korra, but also the mythical safe haven all post-apocalypse stories must have.

Nisha, frustrated by her failed Avatar test, steps up to take down Agam, who reveals herself to be some sort of combo sandbender/mudbender, and an advanced one at that. So naturally, Nisha reveals herself as the Avatar; and just as she does, the red diamond Anomaly busts through. The Faceless escape in the resulting panic, Pavi manages to lure the red diamond away, and in the aftermath, Jae betrays the White Lotus, resulting in their arrest. New Ba Sing Se and Akasha withdraw their aid, while the Chancellor of Ellora essentially puts the town under martial law.

In the midst of all this, we get two eye-opening visions via the red diamond: Nisha sees a rock with an anomaly crystal sticking out of it; and Pavi is taken to a starfield, where something that is not Rainbow Road forms, leading her to the red symbol of Ellora with six additional circles stretching out into space. As we discussed last week, it’s seeming more and more likely that the goal here is for Pavi and Nisha to unlock the Chakras of the planet, starting with defeating “fear” in Ellora via the Root Chakra — likely specifically tied to the crystal seen in Nisha’s vision. Each “Haven” is actually a place where the Chakra is locked, which will send Pavi and Nisha out into the world once they realize what their “Avatar bringing balance” mission is actually all about.

Those are the broad strokes of the plot, but we skipped over something we mentioned earlier: how funny these episodes are at the same time — Jae calling hay his “nose nemesis,” the “who’s that?” as Pavi tells the citizens of Ellora that everything is going to be okay, and we’ll get into this more in the next section, but everything with the Pudding Guy (Eric Bauza) is laugh out loud funny. And isn’t that one of the big draws of the Avatar franchise, that goofball moments can sit right alongside “heck yeah” moments like Nisha saying “I’m the Avatar?”

It’s thrilling to have this feeling back, and this group of episodes definitely feels like Seven Havens firing on all cylinders. It’s also wild to think there are four more episodes to go next week, when “The Envoys: Part Two” in particular has big penultimate-episode-of-the-season energy. We’ll see you back here then (though there’s more article after this, so hang out one second, will you?)!

Avatar Easter Eggs, References, And Connections

We didn’t mention this last week, but while we’re throwing theories out there, there’s been a lot of hay (my nose nemesis!) made out of the fact that Pavi and Nisha are animated with diamond pupils instead of the oval-esque pupils the rest of the characters have. How does this connect to the Red Diamond? And does it connect to Raava and Vaatu (the spirits of order and chaos, respectively) who both have diamond-ish patterns in them? The show has been slow playing the big mythology moves, but with the introduction of the Spirit energy tentacles this episode, it seems likely this does tie to the two spirits in some way. How? We’ll just have to wait and see.

After Pavi opens up the hole in the crystal in “What Lies Beneath,” we get a mention of a rare sect of earthbenders who can feel things under the ground. While it didn’t start with Toph in The Last Airbender, this is a seismic sense (sort of like sonar) that she taught to Aang and passed down to her daughter, Lin Beifong, who appeared in The Legend of Korra. Does this mean that Pavi and Nisha are tied in some way to the Beifong family tree? Maybe!

Businessman Varrick invented “movers,” aka movies, back in Legend of Korra, and it looks like they developed from black-and-white/sepia-toned to color movers at some point, as we get to see Korra and Asami in all their older glory underneath Ellora.

On the lockers next to the main chamber under Ellora, we get to see a Korra action figure, as well as posters for Aang, Kyoshi, and Kuruk. Notably, Kuruk is getting his own spin-off (as announced at New York Comic Con), albeit from his younger days as a 14-year-old wild child in Avatar Kuruk: Waves of Chaos.

After Pavi connects with the Anomaly under Ellora, we see the older Korra using her glider — which was introduced in Legend of Korra Book 3 — to head from Air Temple Island to Republic City. There, while the Spirit energy tentacles are causing the Cataclysm and Korra is clearly in the Avatar state (check out her white eyeballs), it’s notable that Republic City is otherwise empty. Perhaps this cataclysm wasn’t as cataclysmic as everyone thinks?

At the end of Episode 7, as mentioned, we get that Mad Max scene. Some additional details are that the former Earthbending city of Ba Sing Se has somehow been inverted; they now live on Feather Mountain (a new location), and are airbenders – and historians – riding on Flying Bison? Meanwhile, Akasha (another new location) is the one place that has figured out how to keep using technology from Korra’s time, which means they have a riff on Link’s Master Cycle Zero from Breath of the Wild. Adding in the teases of spirit energy, if the whole world was relying on it and that caused the Cataclysm, it’s likely Akasha has figured out an alternative energy source that nobody else has access to. They’re also, per the dismissive Flying Bison rider, clearly younger.

Let’s talk about the biggest, most important addition to the lore: Pudding Guy. In The Last Airbender, there was a Cabbage Merchant who constantly had his cabbages destroyed either directly by Team Avatar or as a side-effect of their adventures, followed by him holding his cabbages to the heavens and screaming “My cabbages!” Then in Legend of Korra, the son of the Cabbage Merchant, Lau Gan-Lan, formed a company called Cabbage Corp, which was constantly destroyed. In the absence of cabbage, we’ve got our new “guy” for Seven Havens, and that’s Pudding Guy. He keeps making pudding, singing little songs about his pudding, and then having it wrecked by the Avatars. Is it cabbage pudding? Perhaps. But get ready for plenty more “My pudding!” to come.

In “The Envoys: Part One,” as noted above, we get an additional Haven showing up as part of the Order of the White Lotus: Nutha. While the spelling may or may not be off, Nutha is the name of a Southern Water Tribe citizen who plays a big part in “The Rift” trilogy of Avatar graphic novels. The rep from Nutha is a waterbender too, so it fits.

We also mentioned Republic Forest earlier. Republic City was the height of technology and innovation, so as New Ba Sing Se seems to be an inversion (going from earthbending to airbending), the city is now Republic Forest. As a side note, in the chamber under Ellora where Pavi, Nisha, and Jae see the mover, there are banners for all four bending nations. It seems likely that the cooperative ethos of Republic City spread through the whole world… at least before the Cataclysm.

Oh, and turtle ducks show up! They’ve been in every iteration of Avatar. They’re cute! That’s all we’ve got on this one.

articles.title: 25 Years Since Its Reveal, and People Still Search for iPods “Every Two Seconds” on eBay
articles.summary: eBay has revealed that buyers are still searching for "iPods" every two seconds worldwide, a quarter of a century since they were first revealed.
articles.body:
It’s October 23, 2001. Headline: “Apple Presents iPod” . It promised "1,000 songs in your pocket" and fundamentally sparked what turned Apple into the most valuable electronics brand in the world.

Yet, a quarter of a century later, Apple’s official storefronts bear no trace of it. The iPod Classic was quietly phased out in 2014, and the iPod Touch in 2022, sacrificed to the all-consuming presence of the yearly iPhone release .

iPod is still going strong in the secondhand market, however, at least according to the latest marketplace data from eBay. Nostalgia for the iconic device is clear, with someone searching for an "iPod" on eBay "every two seconds worldwide" .

This renaissance aligns with a broader consumer revolution according to eBay, with 76% of consumers surveyed having shopped secondhand in the past year.

Or, perhaps, this could also represent more evidence for an even greater shift in the tech industry. Stop me if you’ve heard this one before, but everything is rather expensive right now, isn’t it? Groundbreaking, I know. So let’s narrow the scope a little further.

Streaming is front and center for a lot of consumers right now. Whether that’s Netflix and Disney+ for film and TV, or Spotify for music streaming. And there’s a monthly cost attached to instantly stream media; we all know this. But it’s a cost that continues to tick upward, without offering any greater value to the consumer.

For a generation, like my own (I was born in 1997), that grew up curating MP3 libraries in iTunes—or a younger generation that’s, hopefully, becoming ever more weary of digital impermanence—we may have reached a relative tipping point.

The convenience of a Spotify, or Apple Music, or [insert any other music streaming service here] subscription no longer outweighs the price of the service. It used to be cheap and convenient, but now riddled with overbearing AI features, advertisements, and algorithms that heavily dictate listening habits; alongside increasing anxiety that I could lose access to something I love at the drop of a hat. And that’s increasingly applicable across all digital libraries, and not just streaming, where tracks , films , even entire video games vanishing from libraries are now regular occurrences .

Using an iPod to listen to music, rather than streaming on your phone, does start to feel a whole lot more appealing in 2026 and beyond. According to eBay, at least in the UK, you can pick up a Classic iPod for, on average, £45 , an iPod Touch for about £30 , and an iPod Nano for about £20 . That’s not bad at all. Hopefully, at least by what eBay’s data is suggesting, people are beginning to wake up to the fact that access doesn’t equal ownership, and trends in the secondhand market continue to rise for the average consumer.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .

articles.title: X-Files Creator Chris Carter on How His I Want to Believe Director's Cut Dovetailed Into His Second Feature, Queens for a Day
articles.summary: X-Files creator Chris Carter on how his I Want to Believe Director's Cut dovetailed into his second feature, Queens for a Day.
articles.body:
2026 has been an interesting year of independence and creativity for The X-Files creator Chris Carter. In August, Hulu released Carter’s Director’s Cut of his 2008 feature debut, The X-Files: I Want to Believe - Vrach Frankenshteyn, with the title and tone he always intended . And this month, he’s promoting the limited release of his second feature, the self-funded indie, Queens for a Day.

IGN attended a recent Santa Monica screening of the time-twisting, cautionary tale with a defiantly political message, Queens for a Day. Carter and the film’s screenwriter, wife Dori Carter, attracted a who’s who of former X-Files staffers including Darren Morgan, Glen Morgan, Annabeth Gish, Kristen Cloke, and Jeff Cahn.

After, Gish led a Q&A with Carter who confirmed that his 2025 recut of The X-Files: I Want to Believe - Vrach Frankenshteyn dovetailed into preproduction for Queen, and even shared several X-Files collaborators like editor Cahn and production designer Mark S. Freeborn. Specifically, Vrach Frankenshteyn locked in December 2025. In early 2026, Carter relocated to his old X-Files stomping ground in Vancouver, British Columbia where he filmed over a tight 32 days. He then edited with Cahn, locking the final cut around October 9 with the most timely political topics he was able to include.

The X-Files: I Want to Believe - Vrach Frankenshteyn Photos

In an exclusive IGN chat, the recently-turned-70 Carter said it’s been a big year for him creatively, and that he’s pleased that he finally got to revisit The X-Files: I Want to Believe which initially wasn’t received well by the fandom.

“I just felt like I had made a movie and they made me change it,” Carter said of his initial disappointment with Fox’s cuts. “I wanted to make the movie a scary movie. It was a Frankenstein movie. No one ever appreciated, or got to appreciate it as Frankenstein. I actually got to put the title Frankenstein in it, so that was very important to me. We made sure it’s an X-Files movie that draws on the Frankenstein story and that's what I tried to put back into it.”

Carter enthusiastically said he was happy with how his cut was received by critics and fans, though he acknowledges the Mulder/Scully shippers were not pleased with his cuts. “The relation-shippers were not happy that I took out some Mulder and Scully,” he said pragmatically. “But we also just did two [season] reboots and Scully learns that she is pregnant in the last one. So when I went back to do I Want to Believe, I had to keep that in mind, that if this is a movie I want people to watch now, that it doesn't feel dated.”

He explained in the Q&A that the Queen for a Day screenplay was written 30-years ago by Dori, optioned but never got greenlit. Recently, he discovered the screenplay in a box during some housecleaning, so he encouraged her to update her Twilight-Zone styled story about an adult daughter, estranged from her traditional mother. When she gets into a car crash, the daughter wakes up in her mother’s body in the 1950s and gets to live her life literally in her mother's shoes.

“I said to Dori, ‘I think you should do this in the political moment we're living in, and you should make the character a right-wing newscaster like Jeanine Pirro who was on [Fox New’s] The Five,’ Carter said. “And that’s really the genesis of the project.”

In its current iteration in Queen, the daughter is Judge Jerri, a big, brash conservative MAGA news pundit (played by actress Erin Boyes) who goes through a journey of begrudging empathy, coming to understanding her mother’s struggles as a single mother and more generally a disappointed woman in an era that afforded her few independent options. She comes to see where her bitterness has poisoned not only her world, but helped do so in the broader toxic political discourse.

Carter said the finished film scared all the studios and distributors but he’s still working on securing one. “The reason we wanted to do this was not just to tell a good tale, but to raise our fists. We’re angry we are living in a world we don't want to live in, and so this is our response to that. And I should say, this story owes to Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, where Scrooge gets to see the past and present and the future, and what Jerri sees is the future that changes her life.”

He also agreed that Rod Serling’s Twilight Zone was a big inspiration. “I just read something really interesting about Rod Serling, that he kept trying to write things that they wouldn't let him put on television,” Carter told IGN. “And he finally figured out for The Twilight Zone, if you write things allegorically, you can actually put things on film that you wouldn't be able to do.”

Queens for a Day is screening until October 22 exclusively at LaemmleRoyal, 11523 Santa Monica Blvd. News on a wider release and more screenings for Queens for a Day can be found at their Instagram page: @queensforadaymovie

Tara Bennett is a contributing freelancer for IGN covering film and television. She has over 20 years of experience covering the film and television industries with bylines at SFX Magazine, Paste Magazine, and SYFY WIRE. She is a New York Times bestselling author of more than 30 official movie and TV companion books including The Art of Avatar: The Way of Water and The Story of Marvel Studios: The Making of the Marvel Cinematic Universe . articles.title: Microsoft shuts down its 17-year-old innovation lab where Satya Nadella came to see what employees were building; company says: "Spirit of experimentation is now reflected in how..."
articles.summary: Microsoft is shutting down The Garage, the companywide program that gave employees space and tools for side projects and ran its annual Global Hackathon.
articles.body: Microsoft is shutting down The Garage, the companywide program that gave employees space and tools for side projects and ran its annual Global Hackathon. The move ends a 17-year run for an effort that started as a small Office Labs experiment in Redmond and grew into maker spaces across 15 regions, from Vancouver and New York to Israel, India and Beijing. GeekWire first reported the news, citing an internal FAQ, and some Garage spaces could be restricted starting today, October 23.The Garage mattered beyond its workbenches and soldering irons. CEO Satya Nadella was a regular at its hackathons, where employees could put their projects in front of senior executives. Now the internal FAQ tells staff that "the spirit of experimentation that once lived primarily in dedicated programs is now reflected in how teams work every day." Employees cannot take any equipment, tools or materials with them when the spaces close.Microsoft says The Garage will no longer run as a centralised programAccording to the FAQ, The Garage will stop operating as a centralised function, and the impact on each location will vary. Neither the FAQ nor Microsoft has said which spaces are affected, including the flagship site in Redmond.A Microsoft spokesperson said the company regularly reviews how it uses its physical spaces and is making changes to some Garage locations. It declined to comment on what happens to Garage employees.The Global Hackathon's future is also unclear. The FAQ says the hackathon team is reimagining the event and will share more later. Microsoft's public Garage website, which showcased hackathon projects and experimental apps, now redirects to the company homepage.Xbox Adaptive Controller and Seeing AI were born in Microsoft Garage hackathonsThe Garage began in 2009 with the slogan "Doers. Not Talkers." Rather than collecting ideas and funding the popular ones, it backed employees who were already building things on their own. Its profile grew after Nadella became CEO in 2014. That July, it ran Microsoft's first companywide hackathon, which drew over 11,000 registrants from 80 countries.Several real products came out of it. Seeing AI, the app that describes objects and text for people who are blind or have low vision, started at a 2015 hackathon. The Xbox Adaptive Controller grew out of a hackathon project that used Kinect motion tracking. The controller was nearly cut over budget concerns before it shipped, The Verge’s Notepad newsletter noted, and went on to star in Microsoft’s 2019 Super Bowl ad. Employee Tuong Do built Mouse Without Borders, which lets one keyboard and mouse control up to four PCs, on evenings and weekends. Arrow Launcher, another Garage app, later became Microsoft Launcher for Android.Employees link the Garage closure to Microsoft's wider cost cutsThe shutdown comes as Microsoft spends heavily on AI infrastructure such as data centres while cutting costs and jobs elsewhere. On Blind, the anonymous workplace app, a post titled "Amy kills the Garage" drew more than 70 comments, with the poster blaming CFO Amy Hood. One employee wrote that the space was where they met friends and made connections that helped their career.It is also the latest in a string of campus closures this year. In January, Microsoft shut its employee libraries in Redmond, Hyderabad, Beijing and Dublin, describing the shift as a move to an "AI-powered learning experience." Its Visitor Center in Redmond's Building 92 closed a month later.The FAQ thanks the employees, volunteers and partners who built The Garage and says Microsoft will carry its legacy forward in new forms. It does not say what those forms will be.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2077 2.5 Update Secretly Added The Witcher 3 Sword and Cosmetics
articles.summary: Cyberpunk 2077’s surprise 2.5 update added a new dual-wielding playstyle, fresh ways to customize protagonist V’s look, extra quests and plenty more, but players have discovered that developer CD Projekt Red secretly added a range of new The Witcher 3-themed cosmetics, too.
articles.body:
Cyberpunk 2077 ’s surprise 2.5 update added a new dual-wielding playstyle, fresh ways to customize protagonist V’s look, extra quests and plenty more, but players have discovered that developer CD Projekt Red secretly added a range of new The Witcher 3-themed cosmetics, too.

The Cyberpunk 2077: Edgerunners update snuck in some sweet new clothes for V to wear, as well as the professor spectacles Geralt can wear in The Witcher 3.

The Witcher 3 items added in the Cyberpunk 2077 2.5 update:

Boar Carver — a small knife, similar to what Geralt pulls out to take a trophy from beasts.

Sihil Sword — a cool sword with ancient writing down the shaft and spiky rivets across the edge.

The Professor's Spectacles — a mask in The Witcher 3’s Hearts of Stone expansion that once belonged to the Professor. It can be purchased at the auction during the main quest, Open Sesame!

Ursine Jacket — a jacket based on the Bear School gear in The Witcher 3.

Ursine Pants — trousers based on the Bear School gear.

As mentioned by @SynthPotato on X / Twitter, you can access the items at V’s apartment once you get a text from Arianne about a gift. It’s a similar method used for other drops added to the game.

@SynthPotato They also added this knife that you missed (similar one Geralt uses to collect trophies in TW3) — vinal (@vinalxo) October 23, 2026

@SynthPotato They also added this knife that you missed (similar one Geralt uses to collect trophies in TW3)

None of this was included in the official Cyberpunk 2077 2.5 patch notes , which mostly focused on the Edgerunners crossover and a new questline featuring Night City founder Richard Night. Those new Glamdocs look nice though — I’ve always wanted to pimp my chrome and add some color to those gorilla arms.

The Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime just got its second season. Set after the events of the game , Edgerunners 2 features a cast of fresh characters as they navigate the dystopian hell of Night City’s corporation-ruled future. Game director Hideo Kojima made a cheeky cameo in it.

CDPR has also partnered with Paramount to make a live-action movie based on the game. However, the Cyberpunk 2077 movie won’t retrace the game’s steps . Smile 2 star Kyle Gallner said he would love to play V , though the news that it won’t follow the games could mean V doesn’t even exist in the movie.

Every CD Projekt Red Game In Development

CDPR had ruled out Cyberpunk 2077 DLC, so this 2.5 update came as a welcome surprise. Some fans still want a Cyberpunk 2077 expansion , though, and are encouraged by The Witcher 3's upcoming expansion, Songs of the Past, which arrives 12 years after the base game launched. Meanwhile, Cyberpunk 2 is in development, as is The Witcher 4 and a number of other games.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: Douglas and Dublin mayors sign friendship agreement
articles.summary: Daryl Barron and Steven Crellin say they want to "build stronger links" between the two cities
articles.body:
In a move to strengthen ties between two cities separated by the Irish Sea, two mayors have signed a Friendship and Cooperation Agreement.

This week, a delegation from Dublin City Council led by Mayor Daryl Barron visited the Isle of Man to "build stronger links" with the City of Douglas.

He and Douglas City Mayor Steven Crellin signed the partnership in English, Manx and Irish Gaelic - something that has never done before.

The aim of the agreement is to ensure that both cities can work together building greater economic development and tourist links and ensure shared opportunities for young people.

"There are rich Celtic heritage roots between the Isle of Man, Douglas and Dublin and Ireland and we are trying to wove that fabric closer together," Barron said.

He said the partnership was not only about council work but also reconnecting the people of Dublin with the Isle of Man.

He said his mother had fond memories of visiting the island in her younger days.

"What she did as a child is fantastic and I think similarly a lot of older generations in Dublin have been to the Isle of Man in their younger days but not recently so this gives them the opportunity to revisit the Isle of Man or vice versa and relive some of those nostalgic memories with their children or grandchildren," he said.

Crellin said he had spoken to the head of the Steam Packet Company Brian Thomson and Ronaldsway Airport Director Mike Beveridge about making travel connectivity between the island and Ireland more easier.

"We are in the middle of trying to build stronger and better links. The conversations have already taken place and we can see how we can improve travel links and make them more economically viable for the people," he said.

Speaking on opportunities for young people, Crellin said the city was putting together the first Douglas Youth Council.

For Barron, who supports youth development, this message was key.

"This generation is very important and we have a very good youth parliament already in place which mimics the city council chamber, I'm happy to collaborate with the mayor here, to show [him] how we do what we do, and how we go about what we do together," he said.

Welcoming the partnership, Douglas Council Leader, Devon Watson, said it would open doors between schools and colleges, businesses and community organisations.

"Let it help us share ideas about building homes, bringing life to our streets, and creating prosperity that reaches the people who need it most," he said.

He added: "We want our young people to find opportunity, our neighbourhoods to thrive, and our cities to be places where everyone can belong.

"May those who come after us find the journey between our cities easier, the friendship deeper, and the possibilities greater."

articles.title: New electronics reach Iran, but prices soar as gov’t fees, US sanctions hit
articles.summary: Latest smartphones are finding their way into Iran despite sanctions and trade restrictions, but many can’t afford them.
articles.body:
Tehran, Iran – When the latest iPhone 18 lineup was released by Apple in the United States on September 18, it only took a couple of days for the new models to go on sale in downtown Tehran.

That is despite Apple not having a physical presence in Iran due to years of international sanctions, and the ongoing months-long US naval blockade of Iran’s southern ports, through which the bulk of the country’s imports previously entered.

“These things can’t stop a mobile phone seller,” a phone and accessories trader in Tehran’s Charsou Mall, a major electronics hub, told Al Jazeera, asking to remain anonymous for security reasons.

But he explained that the process of bringing in phones has become much more complicated, time-consuming and costly, due to both external pressures and domestic conditions imposed by the Iranian government.

Many electronics manufactured internationally are imported into Iran via Dubai in the United Arab Emirates, but the nearly eight-month-long war with the US and Israel has disrupted trade through the Strait of Hormuz . Iran has also repeatedly attacked the UAE throughout the conflict, and the UAE also announced a halt to trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran on August 19.

Some Iranian traders then pivoted to using passengers coming in from Oman to bring in phones and other items. But after US sanctions on all Iranian airlines – and anyone who provides services for them – came into effect in September, few flights are landing in the country .

“Most of the phones are now smuggled into the country. Many go to Sulaimaniyah and then come in by land,” the trader said, referencing the northeastern city in the Kurdish region of northern Iraq, which borders western Iran.

A similar story has also been true for many other electronics currently found in the Iranian market, including laptops, graphics and processing units, PlayStation devices and even Starlink terminals .

This week in Tehran, a MacBook Air 15-inch M4 sold for the rial equivalent of more than $1,450, about 6 percent higher than an average retailer in the UAE. A one-terabyte PlayStation 5 Slim disc-edition console was going for about $730, or 11 percent more expensive than some retailers in the US.

Things are much worse when it comes to mobile phones.

Mobile phone service on imported devices only works for 30 days if a registration fee to the Iranian government is not paid.

The fee was introduced nearly 10 years ago, ostensibly aimed at fighting smuggling and corruption. The amount varies depending on the value of the phone, with the government charging import duties of up to 6 percent for phones worth below 600 euros ($673), up to 15 percent for phones between 600 and 900 euros ($673 and $1,010), and up to 30 percent for phones with a value above 900 euros.

After adding other levies and “warranties” from domestic companies, extra charges for some phones can amount to more than half of the total price paid.

But even a registered phone cannot be used to freely access the internet, as the government imposes severe internet filtering and shutdowns, while global payment methods are off-limits to Iranians and international firms refuse many services to Iranian nationals because of US sanctions.

According to the state-linked Tasnim news site, about $1.6bn worth of mobile phones were imported commercially during the previous Iranian year ending in March 2026, up to 20 percent of which were phones priced at more than $600. Phones worth $470m were brought in by aeroplane passengers, most of them higher-spec phones. There are no clear figures for smuggled phones.

In mid-August, customs chief Foroud Asgari told state media that approximately one million phones had been imported during the first five months of the current Iranian year, versus 3.16 million in the corresponding period of a year earlier. He said the import value of the phones had fallen by approximately 70 percent.

The government can also decide to stop the registration of phones whenever it deems necessary.

That was the case between 2023 and 2024 for newer iPhone models, which authorities said could not be registered under any circumstance because they were made by an American company and were gobbling up precious foreign currency reserves for imports. Authorities did not take issue with similarly-priced high-end models.

Skyrocketing government charges and local restrictions are making it harder for Iranian customers to afford new phones at a time when the monthly minimum wage and basic government subsidies for an average married worker amount to the equivalent of just $83 in Iran.

The rial, the country’s national currency, has continued on its downward spiral. It changed hands for about 2.64 million per US dollar in Tehran on Monday, slightly improved from an all-time low reached earlier this month.

Prices have been surging across the board, especially for food and other essentials , as domestic mismanagement, war damage, sanctions and blockade squeeze the Iranian economy and make most of the country’s 90-million population poorer.

Afsaneh, a 27-year-old teacher from Tehran, said she has been thinking about replacing her iPhone 13 with last year’s 17 model, but balks when she sees the prices.

“The only way to get it is to sell my current phone, use my small savings and also borrow from my parents,” she told Al Jazeera.

She pointed out that many among her peers and acquaintances are also forced to keep old devices alive by repairing them or replacing parts, if possible, since they cannot afford to upgrade.

“A lot of people are one failure of a major electronic device away from getting into serious debt,” she said.

articles.title: Breaking Down the Future of Disney Lorcana TCG with Co-Founder Ryan Miller
articles.body:
Since its debut in 2023, Disney Lorcana Trading Card Game by Ravensburger has sold over 2.8 billion cards inspired by some of the biggest films in Disney and Pixar's catalog, all while cultivating a thriving community of players that collect, battle, and dream of what's ahead. Today, on the official launch day of the Hyperia City set, we wanted to share our chat with Disney Lorcana TCG co-founder Ryan Miller from D23 as we got an exciting glimpse of the game's future.

The team held a panel at D23 called The Quests Ahead for Disney Lorcana Trading Card Game and we learned a lot of exciting details about what's headed our way this year and beyond, but what I'll remember most about our conversation was how this TCG has become so much more than just a game, but we'll get to that in a bit!

For now, let's break down all the big news!

Illumineer’s Quest: The Great Hunny Rescue

The Hyperia City set is out now and has brought the world of Coco into Disney Lorcana TCG, added a new energy source called Ink Drops, and so much more. The title of this set is also kind of a big deal because the team has created a bustling urban landscape that builds out the game's lore in a fresh way.

"We have novelists, visual developers, and storytellers who just keep leveling up, and I think Hyperia City is a great example of that," Miller said. "It starts with a simple question, what would an urban environment in the realm of Lorcana look like? What would that be like? And then we had them go in and play around in that idea and it was really exciting all around."

A fun nod the team came up with was in the name itself, as it stems from Hyperion Studio, where Walt Disney Studios called home from 1926-1940 and where Mickey Mouse was born. From there, they had fun dividing the city into "distinct neighborhoods celebrating the individual attributes of various Illumineers and glimmers" that call it home.

This idea was then an inspiration for new location cards, so you'll be learning about the city while you play/collect. These include Land of the Dead – Marigold Bridge, Merlin’s Shop and Smithy – Magical Market, Khan Industries – Greenway Landmark, Institute of Technology – Honey Lemon’s Lab, and Khan Stadium – State of the Art.

And of course the locations need to be filled with glimmers, and we were introduced to Minnie Mouse - Urban Visionary, Donald Duck - Taxi Driver, and Mickey Mouse - Best in Town. These glimmers fit the theme of Hyperia City so well and show how the team is smartly integrating beloved characters to fit the set. Oh, and we have to mention that Mickey's card is a tribute to the first words he ever spoke: Hot Dog!

We had the chance to get an early hands-on of Hyperia City, and here's what we said;

"Hyperia City brings familiarity in returning characters, another popular Pixar addition, and a game-changing mechanic in ink drops to end the year," IGN's Mike Mamon wrote. "Characters from Big Hero 6 and The Sword of the Stone are back in a big way, which is a nice touch after the big set rotation, making some of their older cards unusable in the main competitive scene.

"Plus, with another Pixar favorite in Coco being highlighted, the set is very enticing for players and collectors out there. And with ink drops being a pretty major mechanic introduction adding another layer of resource management, it’ll be interesting to see how the meta and deck brewing changes as the competitive season progresses."

Into the Inkdark Set and Collector Boosters

We also learned more about 2027's Into the Inkdark set, which will feature villains like Hades and task players with discovering the Dark Illuminary.

Perhaps the biggest news from this set, however, is that it will be introducing the Collector Boosters. These packs are meant for the collectors out there, as they include 12 randomized premium foil cards, each with a special foil treatment.

There will also be a new rarity - Illustrious - and we got a look at one of them - Maleficent - Biding Her Time - and learned it will be just one of six cards per set, and only 23 of each will be printed. And yes, Miller did confirm that they chose 23 as a nod to the founding year of The Walt Disney Company - 1923!

Miller also eased fears and assured me that this wouldn't change anything about booster packs or how players currently engage with the game.

"The Collector Booster is our way of saying to our collectors that this is a wonderful thing you can be excited about. It you want to really bling out your deck, this is a really good way to do that," Miller said. "It's not going to replace regular boosters. We really want this to just be a special thing that also focuses on the artists, which are featured right above the rarity symbol. We've worked with over 300 artists from around the world, and they are all truly amazing."

These Collector Boosters will be part of every set following Into the Inkdark, and they'll only be available for purchase at Ravensburger Play Hub stores, the Ravensburger Online Store, and select Disney locations.

Disney Lorcana TCG is going to space later in 2027 with the Cosmic Quest set, and we got a glimpse of what to expect with some fun art featuring The Little Mermaid's Ariel and Flounder floating among the cosmos.

I asked Miller what this new biome offers the team, and he said it's another evolution of what they did with Hyperia City in trying to explore new ideas and give the fans something they didn't even know they wanted.

"Narrative and game design, they work really closely together because they're really symbiotic," Miller said. "The game designers say, 'Well, we need these mechanics in the game. How can we best be expressed through story?' And then narratives say, 'Well, we're having a story with a setting, like this galactic setting, how can that fit the gameplay?' From that, they've done some really fun stuff there that I won't be sharing with you quite yet!"

What's the most exciting part for me about Cosmic Quest is that, for the very first time, Wall-E and EVE will be joining Disney Lorcana TCG with Cosmic Quest!

Beauty and the Beast Curator’s Collection Set

Of all the big reveals at D23, I think I was most blown away by the Beauty and the Beast Curator's Collection set. Listen, it's no secret that the art of Disney Lorcana TCG is on another level thanks to some truly incredible artists, and this set is the perfect example of how the team keeps one upping themselves.

This Curator's Collection set, which is the second one following the Heroines Edition, will be released in October 2026 and is part of the celebration of The Beauty and the Beast's 30th anniversary. What sets this collection apart is that the artwork takes inspiration from the movie's stained-glass motif, and these cards are gorgeous. The character art in concert with the colors come together so beautifully, and there is also just so much joy in each of the faces. I know this will be hard to get, but this feels like a must have!

"To me it's a love letter," Miller said of this set. "It's our love letter to our fans, and it's our love letter to Beauty and the Beast. Furthermore, the attention to detail is how we show our love. It's something that Disney exemplifies, and they're the best in the world at this, and that attention to detail is how we show our love for these characters and stories on those cards. You've only seen the video of it, but to hold them in your hands and to see what actually went into these, it's amazing. Our creative team is second to none. They make such beautiful cards."

Speaking of Disney Lorcana TCG's artwork, the Disney Lorcana Visual Guide is on its way to store shelves on February 1, 2027, and is meant for fans who want to dive deep into the lore and/or just admire a collection of art in a coffee style book you can display with pride. This book gathers art from many of the different sets and scales them up so they can be appreciated even more, and I'm all for that!

Disney Lorcana TCG Returns to EPCOT International Festival of the Arts With Figment

If D23 showed us anything, it's that Figment is, deservedly, having quite a moment! In addition to the news that Figment and Dreamfinder will be part of a new iteration of Journey Into Imagination at EPCOT, the team at Disney Lorcana TCG confirmed they will be back at EPCOT's International Festival of the Arts with the first-ever Figment card!

Miller shared that over 170,000 people participated in the first collection quest at the last festival, and Figment spearheading the next one just feels right.

"It's just wonderful," Miller said of finally getting Figment on a card. "At the last festival, they had a Figment popcorn bucket and there was this huge line. It's just so great when a character just brings people together. So, to be able to include Figment on a Lorcana card is just so cool. I also think we found the perfect card for him, and I was really excited to hear the crowd when we revealed it.

"I don't know how else to put it, but Disney fans are so delightful. This Figment love is just so neat to me, I mean, he's not been in a film, but they love him. One of the favorite things about my job is I love, love, love when people are geeking out about stuff they love. And I say this as a lifelong geek, right? I love it. It's wonderful. My eye doctor was geeking out about the veins in my eye and I'm like, 'keep going!' He's like, 'I'm probably boring.' I'm like, 'No, dude, it's super compelling.'"

Disney Lorcana TCG Digital Version + Disney Cruise Line Expansion

To conclude Disney Lorcana TCG's panel at D23, the team shared they are hard at work on a digital version of the game. The goal is to allow players to play how they want, when they want, and where they want in a simpler way.

"For me, there are two main things," Miller said of the digital version. "One is that this is for Lorcana players who, for whatever reason, have a lifestyle change or something like that. If they have a toddler, for example, and can't go to their weeklies as much as they want to, this is for them. Or maybe they haven't found their weeklies yet or just want to practice, this will be an incredible tool for that.

"On the other hand, it's an invaluable tool for learning how to play. A lot of us, myself included, might feel a bit of a social cost when we're being taught by someone. We're like, 'Oh, what did you say again?' Or, 'I don't want to bug you, you're the middle of teaching me, blah, blah, blah.' And the digital game is such a great way to do that; to just learn in a social free environment. I could just learn there and then build up my confidence and my skill level so that I can then feel more empowered to go to a weekly, to go to an event, to simply sit down with somebody and play. Sitting down on the tabletop is so fun, and we're hoping this helps more people get there."

Those voyaging on Disney Cruise Line in 2027 will also have a chance to experience Disney Lorcana TCG as Collection Quests and more will join the fleet, meaning there are even more ways to play!

Disney Lorcana TCG had a huge presence at D23, and Miller shared that this convention will always have a special place in the team's heart as the 2022 show is where the game was revealed to the world.

"Before that moment at D23 2022, we just weren't sure," Miller said. "We had a booth that was probably a 10th of the size of the one we have now, and we just weren't sure. And then the crowd showed up and we had a huge line. It was this wonderful moment for us and it gave a much needed boost, because we'd been working on this project for nearly two years in the dark."

At D23 this year, Disney Lorcana TCG and Ravensburger as a whole had photo ops, a collection quest, a D23 Challenge Championship Qualifier, and, of course, some exclusive, current, and pre-release items for the army of fans to enjoy.

The big ticket item was the 2026 D23 Collection, which included beloved glimmers from past quests and, perhaps most exciting, the first-ever card from the upcoming Hyperia set - Coco's Héctor Rivera. The set also includes Lilo & Stitch's Angel, Pocahontas, Mulan's Mushu, Zootopia's Judy Hopps, and The Incredibles' Mr. Incredible.

As a huge fan of Winnie the Pooh (Happy 100th BTW!), the highlight for me just may have been the Winnie the Pooh - Hunny Wizard Premium Playmat. This gorgeous playmat features premium hunny foil details and stitched edges, and just looks so good in person.

A much-anticipated pre-release item at D23 was the Quest of Wonders: An Illumineers Lorebook. This first-of-its-kind novel not only features incredible art from Disney Lorcana TCG's artists an a stunning Pegasus promo card, but actualy tells a story from inside the game's world.

The story follows Illumineer Shanzay, who comes across an old lorebook and is trying to figure out who it belonged to and why it was hidden.

"The more she reads about the author's adventure—how he set out with his glimmers of Peter Pan and Pegasus in search of his missing mentor—the more shocking her discoveries become, which she records in margin notes," the official description reads.

Such other exciting items on display were some of the Lorcana puzzles, and I was so excited to put together the Winnie the Pooh & Piglet - Hunny Mages 300-piece puzzle with my son as it paired perfectly with the playmat!

There was also the Disney Lorcana TCG: Collection Starter Set - Rapunzel Edition, which comes with 4 random packs, a Collector's Card Portfolio with Rapunzel herself, a Collector's Guide, and a stunning spcial edition promo card of Rapunzel - Ethereal Protector.

Oh, and Disney Villainous is still going strong at Ravensburger, and we were able to get our hands on the Come, We Fly! expansion that celebrates Hocus Pocus' Sanderson Sisters and even comes with an exclusive game piece of the sisters that will be sure to be a treat to any fan of the film.

Disney Lorcana TCG Is Much More Than Just a Game

To end our conversation, Miller and I just spoke for a few moments about what Disney Lorcana TCG really means to the players around the world. As with many of the things they love, they become so much more than what they appear on the surface because of the memories and moments we create with them with the ones we love.

"I'm just so proud to be a part of something that could make people this happy," Miller said with a big smile on his face. "I'm also just so proud of this team. They have done so many fantastic things in a short amount of time, and I'm really proud to be a part of that too. What we're doing here is special, and we're not here to squeeze the juice out of the grapes. We're here because we want to grow the vines. We want to grow more grapes. It's a long process, but it's really important."

And those vines have spread in ways the team could never have predicted, and I have one final story to share with you from Miller that sums it all up perfectly.

"There was a fellow I was talking to earlier today who was a special education teacher," Miller said. "He was at one of his locals when a kid came in with his parent who wasn't really engaging or anything like that, and he taught this kid how to play. Now, this kid has totally come out of his shell and has become a competitor and a really good player. This was his thing now. It was something that he could really own and it was his deal. And I just love that because who knows what else could happen? It's just wonderful when you send ripples out in the world and some of them come back. It's just a wonderful thing."

articles.title: 'I Don't Know if There's Perfecting It' — Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Multiplayer Chief Weighs in on Matchmaking
articles.summary: Infinity Ward's Multiplayer boss weighs in on Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 matchmaking.
articles.body:
The Call of Duty matchmaking debate has raged on pretty much since the beginning of multiplayer. Should matches be comprised of evenly skilled players, if there’s an accurate enough way of ensuring that? Or should skill be stripped out of the equation, so you never know what to expect from the next match?

Both sides of the argument have their valid reasons for their preference, but most recently, in 2025’s Black Ops 7, an option was presented that attempted to satisfy all. While the default matchmaking was set to skill-based, as has been the case since 2007’s game-changing Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, open matchmaking playlists were also available to those who want the opportunity to get teamed up with, and against, anybody.

This year’s Modern Warfare 4, though, has launched without that option, once again placing the matchmaking debate into the spotlight within the COD community. Is there any way to keep everyone happy, then? IGN spoke with Infinity Ward's Multiplayer creative director, Joe Cecot, who explained that match quality is the priority.

Call of duty: Modern Warfare 4 Classic Prestige Rewards

“I don't know if there's perfecting it,” Cecot said of matchmaking. “For us, I think the most important thing when we look at matchmaking is that the matches we put together are good matches. And we're also looking at the players and their experience, and we can look at the data and how it affects things, and we can quantify how it affects a certain group of players or a large percentage of them in a negative way. And so, though we're not talking about exact specifics on matchmaking, our end goal is that every match is a good match.”

A fairly vague answer, then, and one befitting of the often-shrouded way that skill-based matchmaking (SBMM) works behind the scenes of Call of Duty matches. As previously noted, SBMM has been part of COD since the original Modern Warfare, but players only really started to feel it affecting their online experience once the algorithms were tightened from the 2019 reboot onwards.

On the surface, SBMM seems like a logical thing to want to employ in an online shooter — evenly skilled players being pitted against each other should make for the most exciting, closely contested matches. But the problem comes when you start overachieving and play out of your skin for a couple of rounds, with the algorithm then reacting and placing you in a much higher skill-level match next time up, only for you to have a miserable time getting your head popped off every time you peek around a corner. In theory, it’s a smart system, but in reality, it can lead to whiplash from one match to the next.

Is there any way to perfect it? Perhaps not. But Black Ops 7’s open queue did at least give players the option to roll the dice and opt out of skill-based matchmaking and join open queues if they wanted to. There’s a spot of confusion among the playerbase as to whether this is included in MW4, though — a persistent lobby option is available within the popular modes tab, but it doesn’t state whether this means open matchmaking is in effect. The fact that open matchmaking seemingly isn’t in MW4 at launch, or at the very least isn’t clearly displayed as being present, is therefore a little baffling.

For more on Modern Warfare 4, you can check out our review of the campaign , which will soon have multiplayer impressions added, or what we think of the extraction shooter mode, DMZ , so far.

We’ve got an in-progress Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Walkthrough to help you through the campaign missions, plus All Collectible Note Locations , and all the Code Solutions you’ll need to open every keypad and container. For multiplayer, check out How to Level Up Fast in MW4 and our Essential Multiplayer Tips and Tricks alongside the Best MW4 Settings we recommend you use. DMZ is back, so we’ve got a handy DMZ Beginner’s Guide , too.

articles.title: Mass Effect-Style Game Exodus Picked a Hell of a Time to Reveal Its Redesigned Male Protagonist
articles.summary: The developers of Mass Effect-style game Exodus picked a hell of a time to reveal their redesigned male protagonist.
articles.body:
Archetype has shown off its updated character model for the male version of Exodus protagonist Jun Aslan. Prior to this, fans had complained about Jun’s “long” face, “beady eyes,” and “botox” cheeks.

“He just looks uncannily plastic surgery filled who's constantly serving his best iPhone face,” said one person at the time. “He looks like chad version of Timothee Chalamet (derogatory),” said another.

With his makeover complete, Jun has gone full twink mode, and looks a bit like Leon Kennedy’s younger brother. The rough edges have been sanded down and now he looks like he could front a space boy band. Dem cheekbones.

Fans on Reddit seem much happier. “Not a huge fan of the default hair TBH but I can change that so all's good — the facial structure has really improved,” said one poster . “OHHHHH that is so much better. He looks like a dashing space hero instead of a bad go in the character creator, which is perfect,” said another .

The timing of this new trailer is interesting. Players are looking at Exodus and Owlcat's The Expanse: Osiris Reborn as spiritual successors to the dormant Mass Effect series. Exodus is clearly inspired by Mass Effect, putting you in the shoes of a ship captain making tough choices across alien worlds. It also puts an emphasis on relationships with your crew, who you can bump uglies with . Indeed, former Mass Effect developers, such as lead writer Drew Karpyshyn, are working on the game.

With EA announcing Mass Effect developer BioWare’s closure and the cancelation of Mass Effect 5 this week, this Exodus announcement feels like a timely reminder that space RPGs are still very much on the menu, and BioWare lives on in spirit at other studios.

Exodus Male Protagonist Visual Update Screenshots

Exodus fans have picked up on this, too, with some pointing to the Jun reveal coming hot on the heels of the leaked Mass Effect 5 trailer , which suggested a Mass Effect Universe title for the canceled game. "Who is here after watching the leaked Mass Effect Universe trailer?" one Exodus fan said . "I purposely watched the Universe trailer first and Exodus last so I'd feel a little better," another said.

"Great timing Archetype!!!" one person commented. "This couldn’t have been revealed at a better time with the fallout of BioWare’s closure. The cheekbones really were the issue I think and this new, younger looking model really addresses it plainly and completely. Hopefully this satisfies the complainers who have made such a rabble about Jun’s face!"

When you play Jun Aslan, you choose whether they are male or female, with options like hairstyles, hair color, facial hair, and tattoos available to the player. Archetype has yet to reveal 'FemJun,' but did promise we'll see her soon. "We’ve got something special cooking for her reveal, and we think it’ll be worth the wait," Archetype teased.

Archetype promises a dark story where your actions have a massive impact on the world around you, with branching dialog trees where your choices matter. A butterfly flaps its wings on one planet, and a bit of space dust sticks in a dude’s eye lightyears away. Exodus is planned for launch on April 7, 2027, for PS5, Xbox Series X and S, and PC.

articles.title: Franchises Like Mass Effect Are a 'Prestige Project' for EA, and BioWare's Closure Was 'Entirely Predictable,' Analysts Say
articles.summary: Games industry analysts told IGN that BioWare was likely doomed well before EA’s $55 billion acquisition, explaining that games like Mass Effect are now considered “prestige projects” for the company, and it’s unlikely the sci-fi franchise, nor BioWare’s other IPs, are sold off.
articles.body:
Games industry analysts told IGN that BioWare was likely doomed well before EA’s $55 billion acquisition, explaining that games like Mass Effect are now considered “prestige projects” for the company, and it’s unlikely the sci-fi franchise, nor BioWare’s other IPs, are sold off.

On October 21, EA announced a major shift in strategy and a significant internal restructuring that involves the cancelation of a number of projects, the closure of BioWare , and a reported 400 people losing their jobs. The Canadian studio, known for franchises like Mass Effect and Dragon Age, was shut down after more than 30 years of creating beloved role-playing games. Mass Effect fans must now consider that the franchise is dead — something the leaked internal trailer for Mass Effect Universe made all the more difficult to accept.

Needless to say, Mass Effect fans were gutted by the news, hoping against hope that EA might sell off BioWare’s IP rather than letting them languish in obscurity. But analysts have expressed doubt that outside companies will take on BioWare's franchises, even as EA faces down a massive debt incurred by its acquisition.

11 Mass Effect Characters and Moments the TV Show Needs to Be a Hit

When asked about this possibility, industry analyst Joost van Dreunen said, “maybe,” but explained that these IPs are likely far too costly — and far too time-consuming — for other developers to tackle.

“In many ways, BioWare's IP is in the same boat as some of the other studios we recently saw being divested. They are all well-known and too expensive for most buyers. Capable publishers like CD Projekt Red already have their hands full with their own projects,” he said. (He’s not wrong; CDPR certainly has a lot on its plate right now, what with The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 being in active development.)

The next Mass Effect was announced six years ago, at The Game Awards 2020, and this time last year Mike Gamble, now former executive producer of Mass Effect at BioWare, celebrated N7 Day to say the game was still in development. He even expressed excitement about the Amazon TV series ( which IGN understands is currently still in the works ), and insisted EA and BioWare "remain committed to telling more stories in this universe."

So what changed? Why cancel Mass Effect 5 now? Van Dreunen told us that, in EA’s eyes, legacy IPs like Mass Effect are likely being viewed as “prestige projects,” and the future looks grim for other development teams still underneath EA’s umbrella.

"Before its buyout, EA had been focusing on building recurring revenue streams, and the focus of its new owners is sports, live service, and new markets like Asia. Even if Mass Effect and Dragon Age were fantastically successful, corporate will insist on predictable cash flow. It makes franchises like Mass Effect a prestige project,” he continued.

“Considering the debt load, I'd expect to hear about more layoffs in the months to come. The memo already shrinks the skate. team and pauses a project for The Sims. I expect EA's town hall in November to bring more bad news."

Van Dreunen, along with fellow analyst Piers Harding-Rolls of Ampere, considers BioWare’s closure an inevitable consequence of EA’s current business structure, calling it “entirely predictable and precisely what a leveraged buyout looks like once the deal closes.

“In this case, EA now carries roughly $18 billion in debt, which costs it about $1.8 billion a year in interest. That is more than its annual EBITDA of around $1.5 billion. EA has told its lenders it will cut $700 million in annual costs to service the debt. In that context, a 50-person team working on a game that is years from launch is the easiest line to cut, regardless of its legacy,” van Dreunen said.

“This news is emotive for many adult gamers because of Bioware’s long history of delivering games with deep narratives that connect with audiences, meaning it has a large cultural footprint. It’s a name that has been around for 30 years, so seeing it close is a significant moment for the industry. In particular, the original Baldur’s Gate games, Neverwinter Nights, and KOTOR were genre defining, and the later Mass Effect titles also strongly resonated with audiences,” Harding-Rolls told us.

Harding-Rolls added that the commercial failure of BioWare's last game, Dragon Age: The Veilguard, played a part in BioWare's demise. And let's remember that 2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda and 2019's Anthem also failed to meet EA's expectations.

“Unfortunately, the studio’s recent big-budget releases have not performed well enough commercially," he said. "Ampere data shows that Bioware’s latest release at the end of 2024 — Dragon Age: The Veilguard — has sold an estimated 1.9 million units globally across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam up to the end of September, way below internal targets. The changing nature of high-end gaming and the need to cut costs means that it is likely that Bioware’s future was under discussion before EA was acquired by the PIF and its partners.”

BioWare: Stories and Secrets From 25 Years of Game Development - Exclusive Book Preview

It's a point backed up by MST Financial analyst David Gibson. “I think the closing is a combination of factors: EA going private and needing to improve returns and margins to fund large debt, high relative costs in the West (versus Asia, etc.) to develop AAA games, and role playing games like Mass Effect not doing enough sales to be profitable enough,” he explained.

“It appears there were many other games in development using IP which were also scrapped. I would hope a small and nimble studio would acquire some of the IP and make great games that users love and that contain innovation, rather than repeat the same stuff. EA has a history of making a series of games that are just not fun to play or contain innovation.”

Whether or not EA ends up selling off BioWare’s IP remains to be seen. Former BioWare executive producer Mark Darrah is more optimistic about this possibility than he was previously, but remains skeptical, saying EA could be just as likely to “forget they ever existed and bury them in the vault.”

We have much more on the dramatic news of BioWare's closure, including reaction from fans and the video game industry , and IGN's Ryan McCaffrey on why BioWare was the greatest RPG developer ever .

articles.title: PlayStation Is Offering $40 Off PS5 Refurb Bundles Ahead of GTA 6
articles.summary: PlayStation is offering $40 off when you buy a refurbished PS5 console and DualSense controller together, delivering up to $155 in total savings.
articles.body:
PS5 consoles are still a pretty hefty investment, so it's always worth keeping an eye out for ways to make the jump to current-gen gaming a little cheaper. Especially in 2026, and with GTA 6 just around the corner.

PlayStation has a brand new offer that does just that in the run-up to Black Friday, knocking $40 off when you buy a Certified Refurbished PS5 console and a Recertified DualSense wireless controller together. The bundle starts at $518 for the Digital Edition , while the disc-drive model comes to $568 .

PlayStation 5 Console + Additional DualSense Controller

Save $155 on a PS5 and Two DualSense Controllers

Let's break this down a little further, as there are more savings here than it initially seems. With the additional $40 applied at checkout, you're essentially getting $723 worth of hardware for just $568, at least on the refurb PS5 disc edition.

For the digital edition, it's $673 total, down to $518. How does this work exactly - I hear you ask? So, you're already getting a $100 discount on a refurbished PS5 console compared to buying new ($599 / $649 MSRP).

Let's be clear, though: you're getting an additional controller with this offer , not just a discount on the console. You can choose from a range of DualSense controller colorways, too, so there's a chance to pick up a second pad that suits your setup.

A standard DualSense wireless controller usually costs $74 via PS Direct, but the recertified controller in this bundle costs $59, and effectively drops to just $19 after all is said and done. You can also opt for a couple of different colorways such as Sterling Silver or Volcanic Red that are slightly more expensive, costing $64 instead of $59.

That makes this less of a straightforward PS5 discount and more of a great deal on an extra controller.

If you're planning to play couch co-op games with friends or family, having a second pad ready to go is a big plus. It also means you won't need to buy another controller separately later on.

The discount applies automatically at checkout when you purchase both eligible products in a single transaction, so there's no coupon code to worry about either.

And with Grand Theft Auto 6 scheduled to launch on November 19, 2026, it's a good opportunity to get your console sorted ahead of this year's biggest release.

The PS5 is still a very expensive purchase, but if you're planning to pick one up anyway, this offer makes the refurbished route a much easier to consider. And, with the PS5 Pro basically unavailable in the run up to GTA 6, this is the best you're going to get!

Plus, I should mention, that this deal is only live until November 5, 2026, so you've got a limited window in order to take advantage.

Honestly, no. I don't foresee there being any significant console deals in and around Black Friday this year, they are simply too expensive to produce. That's why refurbished is the way to go, especially with excellent deals like this.

Plus, GTA 6 is out November 19, so unless PlayStation drops an surprise discount on the PS5 at the start of November, you're better off just getting your console ASAP to avoid disappointment.

WHO SURVIVES THE FINAL BATTLE BEFORE THE WAR? INFERNAL HULK has gathered his armies, his fortress and now his champions.
